extracted.intended_audience: educators, municipal officials, industrialists, apprenticeship-school directors, and householders selecting small motors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on organizing and evaluating apprenticeship/industrial schools (curriculum, shop practice, staffing, costs) and on selecting small domestic/workshop motors for intermittent household or farm use. Covers pedagogical, organizational, and economic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary aim — make good workmen
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of the school is simply to make good workmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aim is regarded as higher than that of establishing a self-supporting school; practical outcome (pupils pursuing the trade, earning wages) is emphasized as the chief measure of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free/gratuitous instruction and pupil remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: The education it offers is absolutely gratuitous, and even remunerative to the pupils, for they receive every week a 'gratification' varying from a franc and a half to three francs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pupils are not boarders; remuneration and free instruction encourage attendance and practical training without imposing boarding costs on families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission requirement — primary education completed and easy exam
rubrics_metrics.description: None of the pupils are admitted until their primary education is completed, and then only after an easy examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures basic literacy/numeracy before technical training begins while keeping entry accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course length and target ages
rubrics_metrics.description: The course lasts three, or in some cases four, years. The school can receive young lads of thirteen or fourteen, and after a three years' course can turn out workmen at the age of sixteen or seventeen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program length should align with realistic expectations for producing employable, wage-earning workmen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of general and technical instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Five hours a day are given to studies, six hours to the work of the shops. The teaching of the schoolroom is both general and technical in character, mechanics, physics, chemistry, and technology being added to the usual programme of literary routine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mixed curriculum with both theoretical (science) and practical (shop) components is essential; scientific branches may be led by the director to maintain quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on drawing, measurement, and geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: All the apprentices learn also to sketch bits of machinery or even entire machines, figure the sketch from actual measurement, and then with rule and compass draw them carefully to scale. The system of solid geometry taught in the schools is excellently conceived and admirably followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting and geometry are core skills; insist on accurate measured sketches and scaled drawings as part of shop practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop trades and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two principal workshops, one devoted to the workers in iron, the other to workers in wood. The trades actually taught are forging, metal-turning, fitting, carpentry, wood-turning, and pattern-making. A small workshop for teaching the manufacture of philosophical instruments has also just been organized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide separate, well-equipped shops for main material groups and include specialised small workshops where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotational first year to avoid premature specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: During his first or preparatory year the apprentice... is making the round of the various shops, taking a fortnight in each in rotation. There is therefore no haste to specialize his work, and he has the opportunity of discovering the pursuit for which he is best fitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rotation early on so apprentices discover aptitudes before choosing a specialty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive, experience-prescribed task sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: After that he will pass to a task a little more difficult, following the course prescribed by experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure shop work progressively from simple to more complex tasks based on practical experience rather than arbitrary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of working drawings before manufacture
rubrics_metrics.description: No single object must be attempted before the working drawing of it has been made out in plan and elevation; and the niceties of true surfaces and exact angles are scrupulously insisted on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insist that students prepare full working drawings (plan and elevation) before fabricating items; enforce accuracy in surfaces and angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for non-salable practice work
rubrics_metrics.description: The first exercises in carpentry and in turning are literally exercises; useful to the last degree to their constructor, but of no marketable value... Better waste wood, says the superintendent of the shops, than spoil the making of a good apprentice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit wasteful practice in early training rather than forcing production of salable goods that compromise learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of municipal support and private initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: In France many of the schools have been initiated by the municipal or communal authorities. In Germany it is the town or the state that has made the venture. All that is most valuable in the results obtained in the majority of the typical cases afforded by the Parisian schools can also be attained by private local enterprise, if guided wisely and well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both municipal/state-supported and private local enterprise models can succeed; adapt model to local industrial and civic conditions rather than copying wholesale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid prioritizing self-support over training quality
rubrics_metrics.description: It differs from the Institution de Saint Nicolas in regarding the aim of producing good workmen as higher than that of establishing a self-supporting school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let the drive to make the school financially self-supporting override pedagogical objectives and the quality of training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shop supervision and student industriousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Healthy and actively industrious the lads toil at their work, and three foremen suffice for the efficient superintendence of the hundred!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a productive workshop atmosphere with a small number of competent foremen able to supervise large cohorts effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: School daily schedule and non-boarding model
rubrics_metrics.description: From seven in the morning to seven in the evening are the hours of school, with an hour's intermission for dinner, and two shorter recesses. Work over, they disperse to their separate homes, for there is no boarding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt long school/workshop days with breaks; consider non-boarding models to keep costs lower and integrate community/ family life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic metrics and cost accounting
rubrics_metrics.description: M. Muller points out that the cost of setting up these shops... has been at the average rate of $55.75 for each of the one hundred and seventy-five places nominally provided... while each of the present two hundred and twenty-one pupils... costs the municipality on the average an annual sum which is, as it happens, almost equal, namely, 155.50... The school property and furniture have already cost the city of Paris 750,000 francs... and the school is costing it 60,000 francs a year for working expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track capital and operating costs per place/pupil, offset by sums received for work sold and the value of fabricated instruments; use such accounting when planning scale and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trades & equipment can be integrated into businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish such a school in any large business establishment requires little additional expense beyond the salaries of teachers. The Ecole Professionelle... is looked upon as one of the main causes of the prosperity of the concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large firms can host schools with modest additional expense beyond teaching salaries; industry-run ateliers can benefit both firm prosperity and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine selection for small/domestic motors — appropriate power range
rubrics_metrics.description: In most trades the demand for power is for one of from two to five horse and above, and on the farm a serviceable machine could not generally be much if any less; but in the household that desired is rarely above one horse, and generally under it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose motor power to match typical user needs: householders generally need <1 hp, small trades and farms 2–5+ hp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motor requirements for intermittent household/work use
rubrics_metrics.description: The work for which it is needed is generally of an intermittent character, and this necessitates a machine that will always be ready for work, or that can be made ready with but little trouble at short notice, and that is no expense, or but very small expense, when not being used. It needs further to be perfectly safe, economical in use, of low first cost, and to require but little care, and that of a kind which can be given by unskilled labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select motors that are immediately available for intermittent tasks, low-idle-cost, safe, economical, low purchase cost, and maintainable by unskilled attendants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match machine complexity to user skill/context
rubrics_metrics.description: A more complicated machine can, moreover, be used with success in the workshop than in the household, as in the latter it would generally be in the care of attendants but little, if any, skilled in the use of machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor simpler, robust machines for household settings; permit more complex machinery where skilled maintenance is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider multiple power sources and their tradeoffs
rubrics_metrics.description: While in large manufacturing only two machines — the water-wheel and the steam-engine — can be used, for the purpose of these small powers the range is much greater. Wind and water, steam, hot air, gas, and electricity, are all suitable and are all to a greater or less degree available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting a small motor, evaluate available energy sources (wind, water, steam, hot air, gas, electricity) for local suitability, cost, and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Windmill design features for domestic power
rubrics_metrics.description: The chief ones being the addition of a rudder-vane... and a centrifugal governing device by which the canvas sails were furled and unfurled as the wind varied. The canvas sails have given place to light wooden slats arranged radially... The tower is an open-work structure of wood or iron, easily erected and taken down when desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer windmills with automatic orientation (rudder-vane), centrifugal governors for sail area control, wooden slatted wheels, and lightweight towers for ease of erection and automatic response to wind variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide practical procurement information
rubrics_metrics.description: I propose in these papers simply to make a brief description of some of the more promising and successful machines now on the market, and give such information regarding the sizes in which they are made, cost of working, and prices, as will be of value to the householder and others having use for such a power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When advising users, include descriptions of promising machines, available sizes, operating costs, and prices to support informed purchasing decisions.
